outcome.technical: WHAT CHANGED. (1) tests/test_stamp_verification.py: __main__ is now _harness.staged_main over its existing STAGES table (72 blocks); the in-process _cases(check, only)/_selftest dispatcher it replaces is removed (staged_main keeps --stage LABEL in-process); the _SWEEP_GREEN fixture follows the sweep's new budget-line wording. (2) tests/test__deps.py: the single monolithic _cases body is cut, at statement boundaries an AST pass showed carry only shutil/tempfile and the _ck_tree helper across, into ten _..._cases blocks plus the existing _git_path_base_cases (11 STAGES rows, dg-*); _ck_tree lifted to module level, shutil/tempfile imported at module level; the layer-debt section shares a block with the scan-memo section so the memoised default-tree scan is paid once; and the three identical whole-tree register_citation_violations() scans in the citation block (rc16, rc16c, the kinds case; profiled 16.3/16.6/16.4 s) are now one scan read three ways. (3) tests/test__output.py: _cases renamed _anchor_cases, its trailing four calls lifted into STAGES rows, 6 blocks (ot-*), case order identical to HEAD (diffed). (4) tools/check-committed-pii.py: _cases cut at its two zero-crossing boundaries into _domain_cases/_contract_cases/_command_line_cases, plus _moving_cases/_plan_problem_cases/_foreign_cases as rows, 6 blocks (pi-*) in the original case order; main() --selftest goes to _staged_selftest(argv), which reaches staged_main through the tools/_suite.py bridge (from _suite import _harness); the old _selftest is gone, which _suite.runner_problem() reads as not-its-finding. (5) tools/sweep-selftests.py: slot_gate keeps ticket order but no longer waits for a staged head's FULL grant while slots idle - wait(ticket, weight) admits once >=1 slot is free, takes min(weight, free) and returns it; sweep() runs the child with the slots it actually got (STAGE_GRANT_VAR and file_timeout use the held number); budget line says 'hold up to N each'; tt5's label states the deadline can also cut a staged suite admitted late with fewer slots. WHY THE GATE: the baseline log shows head-of-line blocking (a staged suite needing 6 of 8 slots waited, 2 slots idle, everything behind it waited); a simulator fed with the measured per-block times (blocktime of the four existing staged suites, profiles of the four targets) predicted that splitting more suites under the old gate makes the sweep SLOWER (sim 540 s vs 491 s baseline at 8 slots, 904 vs 901 at 4) and that moldable admission recovers it (409 at 8, 696 at 4). NEW CASES in tools/sweep-selftests.py: bg4b (gate admits a staged head at once with what is free; with none free the next ticket waits; never takes more than asked or than free), sb1 (the same four cases written whole and as two staged blocks report the same total through the real sweep, each id once, the split one really ran as blocks), sb2 (the split with one block emptied is red: exited 1, exactly one FAIL naming 'b-block DID NOT REPORT', the other block's two cases passed, tally 2/3); bg4 adapted to the returned slot count; fixture case ids are ka1..kb2 so no fixture line can be read as the outer suite's sb1/sb2. MEASUREMENTS, all with python3 <scratchpad>/measure.py = subprocess.run([python3, tools/sweep-selftests.py]) + getrusage(RUSAGE_CHILDREN), default jobs (8 of 10 cores, M1 Max 8P+2E): BEFORE run 1 in this worktree at HEAD code, start 17:36:05: wall 430.6 s, CPU 2209.9 s, exit 0, 193/193 files, 17151 cases. BEFORE run 2 in the driver worktree (clean checkout of the same base 4805f994, git status empty before and after), start 18:22:52: wall 418.3 s, CPU 2180.3 s, exit 0, 17151 cases. AFTER run 1, start 18:15:32: wall 370.5 s, CPU 2210.3 s, exit 0, 193/193 files ok, 17154 cases. AFTER run 2, start 18:35:43 (20 min 11 s after after-run 1): wall 370.9 s, CPU 2207.7 s, exit 0, 193/193 ok, 17154 cases. Spread: before 12.3 s wall / 29.6 s CPU; after 0.4 s wall / 2.6 s CPU. Per-file case counts identical before/after in both pairs except tools/sweep-selftests.py 125 -> 128 (bg4b, sb1, sb2): test__deps 254=254, test_stamp_verification 317=317, test__output 91=91, check-committed-pii 49=49. Per-file wall in the sweep (before run 1 -> after run 1): test__deps 144.5 -> 53.4 s (2 slots), test_stamp_verification 105.0 -> 52.8 s (2 slots), test__output 16.8 -> 7.8 s, check-committed-pii 67.9 -> 45.1 s; standalone at 6 workers: test__deps 22.6-34.1 s (HEAD monolith 128.1 s wall / 127.9 s CPU, split 110.8 s CPU), stamp 21.0 s (HEAD 83.9 s), pii 39.6 s (single-process 55.1 s / 55.1 s CPU, split 56.8 s CPU; its _moving_cases block is 41 s of five whole-tree scans and was left whole), output 7.2 s. ACCEPTANCE: (1) under 240 s - NOT MET: 370.5 / 370.9 s. The bound is outside this task's files: test_drive_phase.py ran 209.6/209.8 s holding 6 of 8 slots in both after-runs; its 113 blocks measured 1343 process-seconds standalone (243.3 s wall at 6 workers); the sweep's ~2200 CPU-s over 8 slots cannot finish under ~275 s even perfectly packed, and the simulator's ideal (every block of every staged suite one slot of one shared pool, longest first) is 327 s at 8 slots, 261 s at 10. Reaching 240 s needs less work in the critical suites (drive_phase first) and/or block-level sharing across suites, which is a tests/_harness.py change (a replay mode) this task does not own. (2) no suite's case count fell - met (above). (3) total CPU not higher - not demonstrated lower: after 2210.3/2207.7 s vs before 2209.9/2180.3 s, i.e. inside the before-runs' own 29.6 s spread (+0.6% on the means). The rc de-dup removed ~17 s CPU from test__deps (127.9 -> 110.8 s standalone) and the extra block processes spent it back. (4) the sweep's own selftest green - met: tools/sweep-selftests.py 128/128 inside both after-runs and standalone.
